overrides._reason: The Cursor hook's managed block is DELIBERATELY byte-identical to the Claude twin's — one advisory engine, two host drivers — and bkit-gateguard-parity.integration.test.ts asserts that byte-identity. De-duplicating to satisfy this rule would mean extracting a shared module, which no host can require: both files are dropped standalone into a consumer repo with no bkit package on their resolution path. Same opt-out, same reason, as the Claude and opencode twins above. Scoped to this one file (template + mirror) + rule.

networkAllowlistBases() is a one-line apex-collapse over expandAllowedDomains output, called once from bkit-modules.ts. Inlining at the call site would move these branches out of bkit-cloud-env.ts (the unit-lane's measured file) into bkit-modules.ts (covered by the integration lane only) and silently erode the unit coverage floor — verified by CI red on the first inline attempt. Kept as a named export for coverage accounting; same shape as expandAllowedDomains above it.

canonicalRow() is a NAMED CONTRACT, not a pass-through: it is the single definition of the byte-for-byte serialisation the friction prune gate compares against, used by both the store writer and the gate. Inlining JSON.stringify at both call sites to satisfy the rule would be exactly the 'rewire callers to satisfy a lint' that rules.md forbids, and would let the two sides drift apart — the gate guards a DELETE, so drift is not free. Scoped to this one file + rule.

loadNetworkAllowlistBases() runs inside an editor-session hook (PreToolUse), where fail-OPEN is the contract: a corrupt or hand-edited .cursor/allowlist.json must NOT crash the session, and returning the hosts resolved so far is correct behaviour, not a swallowed bug. slop-scan's acceptable shape (log + rethrow) would break the editor; the empty catch IS the fail-open contract. duplicate-function-signatures is disabled for the same six files because the four hosts ship the SAME hook: each file must be self-contained (a hook cannot import from bkit), so the shared helpers are identical by construction. Deleting the per-host host list is what made them byte-identical and surfaced the rule; merging the files to satisfy it would break the one-self-contained-hook-per-host contract, and the slop guidance says not to rewire callers as a lint side effect. Scoped to these six paths (template + mirror per host).

Three fail-open catches on consumer-authored JSON (package.json parse in runLintModule already surfaced via the lint-package-json-malformed advisory above; chmod failure on the dependabot helper surfaced via advisory below; .claude/settings.json parse in enrichClaudeSettingsAllows — install must NOT crash on a consumer's corrupt file). slop-scan's log+rethrow shape would abort install/upgrade on consumer input we cannot fix from here; the empty catch with a comment is the fail-open contract, and each is paired with an advisory emission path. Scoped per-rule to this file.

detectOpencodeProvider's fail-open catches on consumer-authored JSON (package.json, .opencode/opencode.json): a corrupt consumer file must fall through to the default provider, not abort install/upgrade. Rethrowing would make bkit's install depend on the consumer's JSON validity — wrong direction. The empty catch with the 'fall back' comment is the contract. Scoped to this file + rule.
